item.title: Xi highlights Sino-US youth ties before visit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Xi highlights Sino-US youth ties before visit In reply to American students, he voices hope they'll help boost bilateral bonds President Xi Jinping has expressed the hope, in a reply to American university students ahead of his three-day state visit to the United States starting on Wednesday, that young people in China and the US will advance bilateral friendship and cooperation. Nearly 100 students from 10 US universities, including Harvard, had written to Xi about their experiences during exchange programs in China and their willingness to contribute to bilateral friendship. Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students had enjoyed a memorable trip and was heartened by their appreciation of Chinese civilization, their hopes for friendly cooperation between the two countries, and their willingness to serve as envoys of friendship across the Pacific. Xi emphasized that young people in China and the US share the same planet and shoulder the responsibilities of their times. He expressed the hope that the students would work with their peers in both countries to carry forward, safeguard and advance bilateral friendship and cooperation, promote mutual understanding between the two peoples, and help ensure the steady and sustained development of China-US relations, contributing their youthful energy to building a better world. The reply came as China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on Monday that Xi will make his first state visit to the US in 11 years. During the visit, President Xi and US President Donald Trump will hold in-depth discussions on major issues concerning China-US relations and world peace and development, Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular news briefing. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance for bilateral relations, Guo said, adding that reciprocal visits by the two presidents within six months represent a historic milestone. China is ready to work with the US to give greater substance to a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, strengthen dialogue and cooperation, and properly manage differences to benefit both peoples and promote world peace, stability and prosperity, he added. The visit follows Trump's state visit to China in May, when Xi and Trump agreed on a new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, providing strategic guidance for bilateral ties over the next three years and beyond. Since Trump took office in January 2025, the two leaders have held two face-to-face meetings and five phone calls, and have written many letters to each other. Sun Chenghao, an associate research fellow at Tsinghua University's Center for International Security and Strategy, said that tariff reductions and an extension of the trade truce were key areas to watch. Putting earlier trade understandings into practice could help consolidate stability in bilateral economic ties, he added. Closer engagement could also help China and the US address challenges facing the wider world, said Zhu Feng, dean of Nanjing University's School of International Studies, highlighting their shared responsibility to support global peace, stability and development. Zhu said a more stable China-US relationship could bolster confidence in the global economy. He also stressed the importance of dialogue on regional conflicts and other international challenges, in order to help manage tensions and reduce the risk of miscalculation. Both sides need to show mutual understanding and respect on issues involving core interests and sensitive concerns, Zhu said, stressing that managing differences does not mean avoiding them. People-to-people exchanges are another important part of the relationship. Xi has emphasized on a number of occasions that the hope of China-US relations lies in the people and that the future depends on young people. In San Francisco in November 2023, he announced an initiative to invite 50,000 young Americans to China for exchange and study programs over five years. The target has been met two-and-a-half years ahead of schedule. Moritz Kuhlmann, an affiliated researcher at the Asia Society Policy Institute's Center for China Analysis, hailed the initiative as a way to deepen mutual understanding. "We start with small steps, very narrow, very concrete," he said, "and that can evolve into something bigger." zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: APEC firms riding drive of modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
APEC firms riding drive of modernization Foreign companies expand presence, tapping growing demand, innovation With China offering new opportunities through its vast market and continued opening-up, foreign businesses are expanding their presence, tapping growing demand and innovation while using the country as a base to serve markets across Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies. Market watchers said China's modernization drive and economic transformation are giving Asia-Pacific firms greater access to its vast and evolving market, advanced manufacturing capabilities and growing innovation ecosystem, helping deepen regional trade, investment and supply chain ties. Zhang Yuyan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in Beijing, said China's push for high-quality development is giving businesses across the region a greater role in China's transformation. Echoing such a sentiment, Tu Xinquan, dean of the China Institute for WTO Studies at the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing, said deeper economic integration across the Asia-Pacific is also raising demand for more efficient and resilient cross-border supply chains, as companies seek faster and more reliable links between producers and consumers. Against this backdrop, German logistics services provider DHL put its Shenzhen, Guangdong province super gateway into operation at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in late July with an investment exceeding 1.2 billion yuan ($179 million), marking its single largest investment on the Chinese mainland. John Pearson, CEO of DHL Express, said China's role in the global economy has fundamentally changed, evolving from primarily a manufacturing base into an increasingly important hub for innovation and consumer demand. "For companies across the Asia-Pacific region, China's industrial upgrading, expanding consumer market and advances in areas such as artificial intelligence, new energy and high-end manufacturing are creating new opportunities to invest, innovate and strengthen their global supply chains," said Pearson. The trend extends to manufacturers. Japanese industrial conglomerate Panasonic Holdings Corp put a new electronic materials plant into operation in Suzhou, East China's Jiangsu province, in late June, following an investment of 600 million yuan. Haruhiko Kuwata, director of the electronic materials business division at Panasonic Industry Co Ltd, a business unit of Panasonic Holdings, said the new plant will serve as a key production base as the company ramps up capacity to meet growing demand for electronic materials used in advanced applications. Honeywell Technology is also strengthening its innovation presence in China. The United States-based industrial group opened a new innovation center in Shanghai on Sept 1. The facility brings together its latest technologies and solutions across 12 immersive industry scenarios covering energy, smart manufacturing and infrastructure. Foreign direct investment in China's high-tech industries rose 35.1 percent year-on-year to 200.26 billion yuan in the first eight months, accounting for 41.7 percent of the country's total FDI inflows, up 12.4 percentage points from a year earlier, said the Ministry of Commerce. Sam Fischer, CEO of Australian vintner Treasury Wine Estates, said the company will continue to deepen its focus on the Chinese market, with China playing an increasingly important role in its long-term strategy. The strategy is backed by strong sales of its core brands, particularly Penfolds, whose sales in the Chinese mainland market rose 34.7 percent year-on-year during TWE's 2026 fiscal year ended June 30. zhongnan@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Be model patriots, youth urged
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Be model patriots, youth urged Students from Hong Kong and Macao experience Beijing firsthand Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang has called on young people from Hong Kong and Macao to uphold the dignity of the national flag and strive to become model patriots in the new era. Ding made the remarks on Monday when he received a delegation of nearly 1,200 people from the two special administrative regions at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. The delegation is visiting Beijing from Friday to Tuesday under the "Salute the National Flag" program. It comprises flag-raising team representatives from 121 primary and secondary schools and 21 universities in Hong Kong and Macao, as well as about 200 officials from relevant government departments, principals, teachers and staff members from schools and universities. Ding said Hong Kong and Macao are enjoying the best period of development in their history. He expressed the hope that young people would deepen their understanding of the national flag, cultivate a deep love for the motherland and put that love into action. He called on them to uphold the dignity of the national flag and strive to become model patriots in the new era who love the country as well as Hong Kong and Macao. He also encouraged them to bring honor to the flag and live fulfilling lives with the passion and vitality of youth. Ding urged the young people from the two special administrative regions to become builders and successors of the cause of "one country, two systems". During their visit, the delegates attended the national flag-raising ceremony at Tian'anmen Square and visited the Great Hall of the People, the Palace Museum and the National Museum of China. They also toured the People's Liberation Army guards of honor base for a study session. The delegation was divided into six groups to visit primary and secondary schools and universities in Beijing. They also took part in dedicated study visits to cultural, science and technology venues, enterprises and rural communities, among other sites. Kuang Chun-wan, a student at Pui Kiu Middle School in Hong Kong, said he was deeply moved and excited after witnessing the national flag-raising ceremony. "The most impressive and exciting thing for me was singing the national anthem together with our compatriots from Hong Kong and Macao, as well as mainland compatriots in the audience. It made me feel the unity of the Chinese nation and the inseparable bond between the Chinese mainland and Hong Kong," he said. Leong Hoi-cheng, a student at Fong Chong School of Taipa in Macao, said she was also excited about the experience. "It's my first time in Beijing and my first time attending the national flag-raising ceremony at Tian'anmen Square. It is nothing like watching it back at school. Seeing our national flag rise slowly in the capital is something to be proud of," she said. Contact the writers at lihongyang@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Foreign vloggers experience Jin Opera in Shanxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Foreign vloggers experience Jin Opera in Shanxi Foreign vloggers and journalists from Chinese and foreign media watched a performance by Jin Opera artist Wu Lingyun in Yuncheng, Shanxi province, popularly known as the hometown of Guan Gong, on Tuesday. On stage, Wu brought Guan Gong's spirit of loyalty and righteousness to life through a vivid Jin Opera performance. During the event, Wu also taught young performers the postures and movements of traditional opera. Foreign content creators, visibly delighted, stepped onto the stage to try their hand, experiencing firsthand the unique charm of traditional Chinese opera. The visit was part of the "Loyalty and Honor Without Borders" campaign, a global online outreach on Guan Gong culture, jointly hosted by the Cyberspace Administration of Shanxi province, China Daily Website, and the Yuncheng municipal government.

item.title: Three areas with huge potential for Sino-US AI collaboration

IMD professor highlights potential for China-US synergy in AI development Share - WeChat
In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Mark Greeven, professor of management innovation at the International Institute for Management Development, said, beyond competition, there is significant scope for synergy between China and the US in the field of artificial intelligence — particularly in mitigating AI risks, advancing AI for scientific discovery, and integrating software intelligence with hardware manufacturing for the real application of AI. According to Greeven, such cooperation would benefit not only both countries, but the whole world.

item.title: China and US can go beyond differences
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
China and US can go beyond differences Share - WeChat
Twenty-six years ago, an American donated $5,000 to a Chinese woman he had never met. She used it to buy saplings and planted them in the sand, turning barren land into a forest. That's how the friendship began. Their reunion this August in China drew widespread attention and touched many hearts. This story demonstrates that the Chinese and American peoples share common emotions. They can transcend differences, appreciate each other, and build friendships. The hope for this relationship lies in the people.
